text:
alex: deploy-bot flagged a canary p95 regression during the 09:00 UTC rollout, sharing logs and proposing a stepwise throttled revert.
deploy-bot: Canary rollout at 50% (slice/region: eu-west-1), metric alert fired: inference_p95 increased 2.5x over baseline. Suggested action: throttle to 25% or revert to 2.3.1.
alex: I see the same in traces — tail latency spikes tied to kvcache eviction on a subset of hosts. Not a total outage but violates our canary SLO.
maria: Can we do a partial revert (slice-only) to reduce blast radius? Need to confirm which slices are safe to pin.
ops-oncall: I can run the slice revert and coordinate customer comms. Which slice id should we target?
sanjay: Target slice eu-west-1-a first. Command I recommend: 
```
redwoodctl rollout adjust --deployment inference-prod --region eu-west-1 --slice eu-west-1-a --traffic 0 --target-version 2.3.1
```
This will pin that slice back to 2.3.1 without touching other regions.
emily: Agree on stepwise approach. If eu-west-1-a reverts and p95 returns to baseline, then we widen the revert to eu-west-1-b.
alex: What are our automatic rollback triggers? Deploy-bot, did the automated rollback runway trigger?
deploy-bot: Auto-rollback configured: enabled for p95 > 2x baseline sustained for 5m AND error-rate > 0.5%. Currently only p95 threshold met. Auto-rollback preserved for a full-region signal, not for single-slice spikes. Manual action recommended.
maria: Ok manual then. Ops, please execute the slice revert and post the command output here. Notify CS if we hit customer-visible latencies > 300ms above baseline.
ops-oncall: Executing now. 
```
$ redwoodctl rollout adjust --deployment inference-prod --region eu-west-1 --slice eu-west-1-a --traffic 0 --target-version 2.3.1
Applying traffic adjustments...
Pin applied to slice eu-west-1-a -> 2.3.1
Waiting for infra convergence (30s)...
Converged.
```
ops-oncall: Pin successful. Monitoring p95.
sanjay: I'm watching traces; initial drop looks promising. p95 from 680ms -> 220ms in eu-west-1-a.
emily: Can we hold and run canary checks for 10 minutes before moving to next slice? That matches our rollback playbook.
maria: Yes, follow the playbook: 10m hold, verify synthetic prompts, check KV hit rate, and ensure no spike in 5xx.
alex: I'll draft a short customer-facing note for CS in #customer-success: "We identified a performance regression during today's canary rollout in eu-west-1 and reverted a subset of hosts to the previous version while we investigate. No data loss; some requests experienced increased latency for ~10m. We'll provide updates."
ops-oncall: Notifying CS now. /msg @customer-success: Reverted eu-west-1-a slice to 2.3.1 due to p95 regression during canary. Asking them to surface any customer reports.
deploy-bot: Canary safety: since we did manual slice revert, auto-rollback cooldown engaged for 30m to avoid double actions.
sanjay: If after the hold the other slices look stable, we can incrementally revert eu-west-1-b with the same command. If we see regression again, we escalate to full-region rollback.
emily: Also recommend creating a short postmortem note in the release board and tagging runtime-telemetry for a deeper KV cache analysis.
maria: I'll own the postmortem and follow-up action items: (1) KV eviction tuning, (2) add canary synthetic specifically for long-tail KV miss patterns, (3) confirm kernel flags used in 2.4.0 build.
alex: For release notes: add a note about the rollback and that 2.4.0 is under investigation — we should not mark it as rolled out. I’ll update the changelog draft.
ops-oncall: 10m hold started (1729023400). Monitoring dashboards linked: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/infra/canary-rollout
[10 minutes pass]
ops-oncall: Hold complete. eu-west-1-a p95 stable at baseline. Proceeding to revert eu-west-1-b per plan.
```
redwoodctl rollout adjust --deployment inference-prod --region eu-west-1 --slice eu-west-1-b --traffic 0 --target-version 2.3.1
```
ops-oncall: Pin applied to eu-west-1-b. Converged.
sanjay: Post-revert status: region p95 back to baseline, no increase in 5xx. Good candidate to abort the rest of canary rollout.
emily: I'll block further canary advancement and set deployment to paused.
deploy-bot: Rollout paused by user action. Canary progress halted at remaining slices. Auto-rollback cooldown active.
maria: Great. Follow-ups: schedule a deeper test-run against a KV-heavy workload on a staging cluster with 2.4.0, and add a regression alert to catch similar patterns earlier.
alex: Thanks all — I'll prepare a short summary for execs: what happened, impact, mitigation, and next steps. We'll reconvene after the telemetry deep-dive. :thumbsup:
ops-oncall: Noted. Closing this thread and moving notes to the release ticket #INF-5421.
